Heron UT-9: aerodynamic revision

The existing Heron now has a slimmer wing with defined incidence, washout and dihedral, a symmetric horizontal tail, controls that turn on their actual three-dimensional hinges, CAD-contained fuel cells, and flight coefficients tied to the private lab. All 129 solids have a contact path to the fuselage. 436 tests pass.

Inspect the aircraft · Fly locally · Private aerodynamic lab · Native CAD viewer · STEP master · Game GLB

Research translated into design choices

Textron’s Grand Caravan EX specifications provide a class reference: 15.9 m span, 12.7 m length, 4.7 m height, 25.96 m² wing area, 3,995 kg takeoff mass, and 867 shp. Heron remains an original utility aircraft. Its 15.87 m span and revised 26.69 m² wing area are consistent with that role; the reference does not establish Heron’s performance.

NASA’s drag-coefficient treatment requires a consistent reference area. The smaller wing now uses a correspondingly larger estimated CD₀ so the fixed fuselage, gear, struts and pod do not gain an unmeasured drag reduction. The old equivalent parasite drag area is retained. Induced-drag comparisons use equal weight, speed and density because a higher aspect ratio obtained only by reducing area does not by itself reduce induced drag at fixed span and lift.

NACA Report 703 studies how taper, thickness, Reynolds number and washout influence stall characteristics. I tested five twist choices and selected 2.5° washout to move attached-flow loading away from the aileron region. This is a design rationale and a measured VLM trend; the lab does not solve viscous separation or establish root-first stall.

Aerodynamics for Naval Aviators, hosted by the FAA describes how tail contribution, downwash and CG affect longitudinal stability. Heron’s neutral point and pitch damping now depend on its tail area and arm, with explicit estimated tail pressure and downwash allowances. They replace a generic fixed offset from the mass model.

What changed in the plane

  • The wing retains a rounded leading edge, 14% NACA-style thickness and 2% sinusoidal camber. Root chord is 1.95 m; the outer control station is 1.31 m, followed by a rounded tapered tip. Root incidence is 2.5° and reduces to 0° across the outer wing. The existing curved fuselage, cowling, glazing, cargo pod and twisted four-blade propeller are retained.
  • The horizontal tail uses a symmetric 10% section. Wing-root fairings and strut attachment heights follow the revised wing. The fuselage remains 12.67 m long and the aircraft remains 4.70 m high.
  • Flaps and ailerons have rounded noses, recessed fixed-wing pockets, pins and 6 mm end clearances. Their end planes and runtime pivots follow each swept, inclined hinge. The game’s local control rotation therefore follows the same axis as the CAD model.
  • The lab solver now accepts station incidence, interpolates twist and positions its quarter-chord vortices and three-quarter-chord control points consistently. Existing zero-incidence wings retain their previous numerical behavior. Runtime Heron CL₀ and lift slope come from the lab at 0° and 4° fuselage AOA; incidence is included once.
  • Fuel geometry, settled-liquid centroids and inertia now come from two shaped volumes enclosed by the wing. Crew/passenger, cargo and wing mass stations follow the model’s layout. Component masses remain engineering estimates.

Why this washout was selected

Each section-loading comparison uses total CL = 0.7 at 144 panels. Inboard means 0.6–4.7 m semispan; aileron region means 4.86–7.45 m. The built wing lowers peak aileron-region section CL from 0.710 to 0.682, approximately 3.9%, against the new planform without washout. It increases inboard loading. A 1.5° twist candidate has the lowest computed induced drag; 2.5° was selected for more outer-wing unloading, with a small drag cost.

Span-efficiency outputs slightly above 1 use projected span for a nonplanar, discretized wing; they are not adopted as whole-aircraft Oswald efficiency. The game retains an estimated efficiency of 0.78.

Fuel packaging and balance

Each analysis envelope occupies semispan 1.10–5.80 m and the 15–60% chord region, ahead of the control recess. Exact CAD containment is checked against the wing envelope. Each encloses 710.9 L before allowances. Three percent structure displacement, three percent trapped fuel and two percent expansion relative to fill capacity are estimates. Settled-liquid geometry produces 1048.7 kg usable fuel and 32.44 kg retained unusable fuel at 0.80 kg/L. The mesh-integrated envelope agrees with exact CAD volume within 0.1%.

Default loading is 65% usable fuel and 100% payload, totaling 3884.1 kg against the 3,995 kg takeoff limit. Full tanks plus full payload total 4251.2 kg and are rejected by the lab’s dispatch check. Fuel settling moves the liquid centroid inboard as the level falls. These are conceptual analysis volumes; tank walls, baffles, structural load paths and fuel-feed behavior are not designed here.

Private-lab results

The actual browser ran a 17-point −8° to +8° angle sweep and the 24/48/96/144-panel convergence check. At 65 m/s and 4° AOA, 96 to 144 panels change CL by 0.091% and CDi by 0.028%. This establishes numerical refinement for that case. The lab’s illustrative full-aircraft flow is separate from its wing-force calculation.

Both flight-validation and fuel-validation workers now include Heron as the fifth aircraft. Engine-map evidence explicitly labels its turboprop map as estimated. Browser export includes all five planes; Heron’s exported numerical result reproduces the current Bun model with a maximum relative/absolute normalized difference of 7.91e-16, within the 1e−8 comparison tolerance.

The tail model estimates a neutral point 0.3039 m aft of the body datum. Across these four dispatch/low-fuel/payload cases the static margin is 7.15–11.97% MAC. Twelve 30-second disturbance runs use zero wind and no beginner assistance; the largest final-to-initial RMS ratio is 0.124. Four powered stall-recovery probes finish undamaged with at least 8.98 s clear of stall at the end of each ten-second run. These check the implemented model and the declared test-pilot policy.

Evidence boundary

CAD geometry, containment, connectivity, sampled control motion, export consistency and the reported simulations were checked. Main-wing VLM is steady, inviscid and limited to attached flow. Whole-aircraft profile drag, CL limits, flap increments, post-stall behavior, component masses, tail pressure/downwash, propulsion lapse and yaw/roll derivatives remain estimates. This pass does not predict local stall progression, propwash, structural strength, continuous mechanism clearance or real aircraft performance.

Rebuild and inspect

bun run heron:build builds the CAD, connection and motion checks, runtime export, fuel geometry and aerodynamic calibration. bun run heron:check runs the 25 focused asset/realism/envelope tests. bun run heron:study repeats the five-candidate wing study. bun scripts/report-heron-aerodynamics.ts regenerates this report from the saved passing evidence. Start the private lab with bun run lab:dev and select Heron.
